findings: Non-blocking (confirmed): handleProviderChange keeps the previous model when the new provider's model list is not loaded, so a provider/model mismatch can be persisted and shown as 'Saved'. Consider disabling the toggle until the list loads or prompting for a model.

Non-blocking (likely, low): aiTrustedCommands is now writable from the renderer with arbitrary string prefixes via settings:set; the UI only removes entries. Consider restricting the handler to subsets of the stored list.
Non-blocking (possible): overlapping saves capture 'prev' from the render closure, so a failed earlier save can revert the UI over a later successful one. Consider a sequence counter.
Non-blocking: aiSaveState/aiSaveError are shared between the provider and Tool Calling sections, so an error shows in both cards.
Non-blocking: no automated tests for the new settings:set key validation; behavior verified by code reading only and the app was not run.
